title: Running Away to the Big Rock

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a child aged 5-9 and an adult)

collection.description: A small child is running away from home forever because bedtime is unfair: walk along with them, or offer to carry the mat.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has announced that (subject.he/she) is leaving home forever, because bedtime is unfair. (subject.He/she) has packed: one coconut, a favorite stick, and a sleeping mat rolled up so badly it is mostly unrolled. (subject.He/she) is now marching very slowly towards the edge of the village, checking over (subject.his/her) shoulder to see if anyone is watching. (friend) is watching.

choices.label: Offer to Help Carry the Mat

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Can I come?" asks (friend). (subject) considers this and allows it. They walk all the way to the big rock at the edge of the gardens, which is where "forever" turns out to be. They sit on it and share the coconut. "It's getting dark," (subject) points out, after a while. "It is," agrees (friend). They walk home together. Bedtime is still unfair, but it happens anyway.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (friend) catches up and offers to carry the mat, since it seems heavy. (subject) gratefully hands it over. They walk a little way. "Where are we going?" asks (friend). (subject) thinks hard. (subject.He/she) hadn't got that far. "Home," (subject.he/she) decides, "but the long way." They take the long way. It is very long. (subject) is asleep before bedtime.
